items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the civil practice law and rules and the real property law, in relation to the recording of a transfer or assignment of a mortgage interest
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A8684

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the civil practice law and rules and the
real property law, in relation to the recording of a transfer or assign-
ment of a mortgage interest

PURPOSE  OF  BILL:    To require parties to record an ownership transfer
document with the County Clerk when there is an assignment  or  transfer
of  the  ownership  of  the  legal  documents  which convey the right to
receive mortgage payments.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS OF BILL:  The bill would amend subdivision (a)  of
§8021  of  the Civil Practice Law and Rules by adding a new paragraph 12
to access a $10 fee to record a transfer or  assignment  of  a  mortgage
interest.  The  fees would be dedicated to the Legal Services Assistance
Fund established under §98-C of the State Finance Law.

It would amend the Real Property Law by adding a new §291-i which  would
require  all  parties  with  recorded  property  interests to record all
transfer or assignments the ownership of  the  legal  instruments  which
convey  the  right to receive mortgage payments due on a mortgage from a
previous owner of the legal instruments to  a  new  owner.  The  parties
would  not be required to re-record the mortgage, pay a mortgage record-
ing tax, or the mortgage transfer tax.  The  recording  party  would  be
required  to pay the $10 dollar fee for the form and the applicable per-
page recording fee.

The recording would be accomplished through use of a "transfer of owner-
ship foist" to be created by the Secretary of State under the provisions
of this legislation. Failure to record  each  transfers  or  assignments
would  subject violators to a civil penalty of $500 for a first offense,
$1,000 for a second offense and $1,500 thereafter, These penalties would
be assessed by the County Clerk and used to support County  Clerk  oper-
ations.  The County Clerk may not issue a certificate of discharge until
all fees and penalties are paid and the public record is brought  up  to
date.

JUSTIFICATION:  The recording statutes have been eclipsed by the passage
of  time and no longer contain a complete public record of the ownership
of real property. The changing business practices of the mortgage indus-
try have led to the free trading of the legal instruments  which  repre-
sent  the  right  to  collect  the stream of mortgage payments from real
property borrowers. Private record keeping entities  keep  a  real  time
record  of  such  transactions to facilitate real time trading. However,
the recording statutes have  been  interpreted  by  the  courts  as  not
requiring  parties to record ownership interests. Thus, borrowers can no
longer ascertain the identity of the owners) of their  promissory  notes
through simple access to the public record. This prevents ready communi-
cation  between  the homeowner and the owner of their legal instruments.
In this time of turmoil in housing and mortgage lending, this  inability
to contact the actual owner of their promissory notes requires an update

to  the  recording statutes so they can once again perform their purpose
of recording the ownership interests of real property.

In  order  for these amendments to the recording statutes to be meaning-
ful, each new owner of the legal instruments will be required to  record
their name - whether business or personal, the address and current phone
number on the transfer or assignment form and that any agent of such new
owner who physically records such interest must record the assignment or
transfer in the name of the actual owner.

The  fees generated by this commonsense update to the recording statutes
will accrue to the benefit of the Legal Services Assistance Fund  estab-
lished  pursuant  to §98-C of the State Finance Law. To ensure that this
requirement is obeyed by the mortgage industry, a failure to record  all
transfers and assignments within ten business days will subject each new
owner  to  an escalating series of civil penalties. The new fees and the
civil penalties are not to be  accessed  upon  homeowners.  Instead  the
requirement  would fall upon the legal instrument owners who are trading
the paper. To ensure that the mortgage  industry  complies,  the  County
Clerk  is  required to withhold the discharge of mortgage until all fees
and penalties are paid and the record is corrected in  full.  All  civil
penalties  will  be accessed and collected by the County Clerk and dedi-
cated to the support of County Clerk operations.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New bill, 2009.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:  Undetermined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  The act will take effect ninety days after becoming law
and shall apply to all assignments and transfers on or after such date.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the real property law, in relation to the recording of a transfer or assignment of a mortgage interest
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A8684A                 REPLACEMENT 5/21/10

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the real property law, in
relation to the recording of a transfer or assignment of a mortgage
interest

PURPOSE OF BILL:
To require parties to record an ownership transfer document with the
County Clerk or City register when there is an assignment or transfer
of the ownership of the mortgage note which convey the right to
receive mortgage payments.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS OF BILL:
It would amend the Real Property Law by adding a new section 291-i
which would require all parties with recorded property interests to
record all transfer or assignments the ownership of the mortgage note
from a previous owner of the legal instruments to a new owner. The
parties would not be required to re-record the mortgage, pay a
mortgage recording tax, or the mortgage transfer tax. The recording
party would be required to pay the applicable per-page recording fee.
The recording would be accomplished through use of a "transfer of
ownership form".

JUSTIFICATION:
The recording statutes have been eclipsed by the passage of time and
no longer contain a complete public record of the ownership of real
property. The changing business practices of the mortgage industry
have led to the free trading of the legal instruments which represent
the right to collect the stream of mortgage payments from real
property borrowers. Private record keeping entities keep a real time
record of such transactions to facilitate real time trading. However,
the recording statutes have been interpreted by the courts as not
requiring parties to record ownership interests. Thus, borrowers can
no longer ascertain the identity of the owner(s) of their promissory
notes through simple access to the public record. This prevents ready
communication between the homeowner and the owner of their legal
instruments. In this time of turmoil in housing and mortgage lending,
this inability to contact the actual owner of their mortgage note
leaves a distressed borrower unable to contact their note owner. This
situation requires an update to the recording statutes so they can
once again-perform their purpose of recording the ownership interests
of real property.

In order for these amendments to the recording statutes to be
meaningful, each new owner of the legal instruments will be required
to record their name - whether business or personal, the address and
current phone number on the transfer or assignment form and that any
agent of such new owner who physically records such interest must
record the assignment or transfer in the name of the actual owner.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: 2009: A.8684-A - Assembly Rules.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:
Undetermined.


EFFECTIVE DATE:
The act will take effect ninety days after becoming law and shall
apply to all assignments and transfers on or after such date..

summary: Requires a recording officer not to record or accept a transfer or assignment of interest in a mortgage unless accompanied with a mortgage ownership assignment document.
